name: The Hibbard household at 1701 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_hibbard_mrs_william_gold

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 1701 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 1701 Mrs. William Gold Hibbard; Frank Hibbard; Mrs. O. Van Schaack Ward.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 1701, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. A house of this kind kept live-in staff, and the 1900 and 1910 censuses name them; neither was read for this card, so no staff are listed. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: Mrs. O. Van Schaack Ward
persons.note: Listed at 1701 in both editions. The Blue Book does not say how she was related to Mrs. Hibbard.

persons.name: Frank Hibbard
persons.note: First listed at 1701 in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904); the 1904 edition does not list him, so whether he was already here on 1 July 1904 is not documented. His relation to Mrs. Hibbard is not printed.
